\maketitle


\begin{abstract}
\texttt{WHIZARD} is an application of the \texttt{VAMP} algorithm:
Adaptive multi-channel integration and event generation. The bare
\texttt{VAMP} library is augmented by modules for Lorentz algebra,
particles, phase space, etc., such that physical processes with
arbitrary complex final states [well, in principle\ldots] can be
integrated and \emph{unweighted} events be generated.  
\end{abstract}

\chapter{Utilities}

These modules are intended as part of WHIZARD, but in fact they are
generic and could be useful for any purpose.

The modules depend only on modules from the {\tt{}basics} set.
\begin{description}
\item[file\_utils]
  Procedures that deal with external files, if not covered by Fortran
  built-ins.
\item[file\_registries]
  Manage files that are accessed by their name.
\item[string\_utils]
  Some string-handling utilities.  Includes conversion to C string.
\item[format\_utils]
  Utilities for pretty-printing.
\item[format\_defs]
  Predefined format strings.
\end{description}

\section{File Utilities}

This module provides miscellaneous tools associated with named
external files.  Currently only:
\begin{itemize}
\item
  Delete a named file
\end{itemize}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{2}\moddef{\code{}file{\char95}utils.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module file_utils

  use io_units

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}File utils: public\RA{}

contains

\LA{}File utils: procedures\RA{}

end module file_utils
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{3}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Deleting a file}
Fortran does not contain a command for deleting a file.  Here, we
provide a subroutine that deletes a file if it exists.  We do not
handle the subtleties, so we assume that it is writable if it exists.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{4}\moddef{File utils: public}\endmoddef
  public :: delete_file
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{5}\moddef{File utils: procedures}\endmoddef
  subroutine delete_file (name)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical :: exist
    integer :: u
    inquire (file = name, exist = exist)
    if (exist) then
       u = free_unit ()
       open (unit = u, file = name)
       close (u, status = "delete")
    end if
  end subroutine delete_file
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{6}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{File Registries}

This module provides a file-registry facility.  We can open and close
files multiple times without inadvertedly accessing a single file by two
different I/O unit numbers.  Opening a file the first time enters it
into the registry.  Opening again just returns the associated I/O
unit.  The registry maintains a reference count, so closing a file
does not actually complete until the last reference is released.

File access will always be sequential, however.  The file can't be
opened at different positions simultaneously.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{7}\moddef{\code{}file{\char95}registries.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module file_registries
  
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}File registries: public\RA{}

\LA{}File registries: types\RA{}

contains
  
\LA{}File registries: procedures\RA{}

end module file_registries
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{8}\nwdocspar
\subsection{File handle}
This object holds a filename (fully qualified), the associated
unit, and a reference count.  The idea is that the object should be
deleted when the reference count drops to zero.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{9}\moddef{File registries: types}\endmoddef
  type :: file_handle_t
     type(string_t) :: file
     integer :: unit = 0
     integer :: refcount = 0
   contains
   \LA{}File registries: file handle: TBP\RA{}
  end type file_handle_t
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{10}Debugging output:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{11}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\endmoddef
  procedure :: write => file_handle_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{12}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\endmoddef
  subroutine file_handle_write (handle, u, show_unit)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    logical, intent(in), optional :: show_unit
    logical :: show_u
    show_u = .false.;  if (present (show_unit))  show_u = show_unit
    if (show_u) then
       write (u, "(3x,A,1x,I0,1x,'(',I0,')')")  &
            char (handle%file), handle%unit, handle%refcount
    else
       write (u, "(3x,A,1x,'(',I0,')')")  &
            char (handle%file), handle%refcount
    end if
  end subroutine file_handle_write
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{13}Initialize with a file name, don't open the file yet:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{14}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: init => file_handle_init
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{15}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine file_handle_init (handle, file)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(out) :: handle
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: file
    handle%file = file
  end subroutine file_handle_init
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{16}We check the {\tt{}refcount} before actually opening the file.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{17}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: open => file_handle_open
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{18}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine file_handle_open (handle)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(inout) :: handle
    if (handle%refcount == 0) then
       handle%unit = free_unit ()
       open (unit = handle%unit, file = char (handle%file), action = "read", &
            status = "old")
    end if
    handle%refcount = handle%refcount + 1
  end subroutine file_handle_open
    
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{19}Analogously, close if the refcount drops to zero.  The caller may
then delete the object.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{20}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: close => file_handle_close
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{21}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine file_handle_close (handle)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(inout) :: handle
    handle%refcount = handle%refcount - 1
    if (handle%refcount == 0) then
       close (handle%unit)
       handle%unit = 0
    end if
  end subroutine file_handle_close
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{22}The I/O unit will be nonzero when the file is open.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{23}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: is_open => file_handle_is_open
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{24}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function file_handle_is_open (handle) result (flag)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    logical :: flag
    flag = handle%unit /= 0
  end function file_handle_is_open
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{25}Return the filename, so we can identify the entry.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{26}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: get_file => file_handle_get_file
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{27}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function file_handle_get_file (handle) result (file)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    type(string_t) :: file
    file = handle%file
  end function file_handle_get_file
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{28}For debugging, return the I/O unit number.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{29}\moddef{File registries: file handle: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: get_unit => file_handle_get_unit
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{30}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function file_handle_get_unit (handle) result (unit)
    class(file_handle_t), intent(in) :: handle
    integer :: unit
    unit = handle%unit
  end function file_handle_get_unit
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{31}\nwdocspar
\subsection{File handles registry}
This is implemented as a doubly-linked list.  The list exists only
once in the program, as a private module variable.

Extend the handle type to become a list entry:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{32}\moddef{File registries: types}\plusendmoddef
  type, extends (file_handle_t) :: file_entry_t
     type(file_entry_t), pointer :: prev => null ()
     type(file_entry_t), pointer :: next => null ()
  end type file_entry_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{33}The actual registry.  We need only the pointer to the first entry.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{34}\moddef{File registries: public}\endmoddef
  public :: file_registry_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{35}\moddef{File registries: types}\plusendmoddef
  type :: file_registry_t
     type(file_entry_t), pointer :: first => null ()
   contains
   \LA{}File registries: file registry: TBP\RA{}
  end type file_registry_t
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{36}Debugging output.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{37}\moddef{File registries: file registry: TBP}\endmoddef
  procedure :: write => file_registry_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{38}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine file_registry_write (registry, unit, show_unit)
    class(file_registry_t), intent(in) :: registry
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: show_unit
    type(file_entry_t), pointer :: entry
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit)
    if (associated (registry%first)) then
       write (u, "(1x,A)")  "File registry:"
       entry => registry%first
       do while (associated (entry))
          call entry%write (u, show_unit)
          entry => entry%next
       end do
    else
       write (u, "(1x,A)")  "File registry: [empty]"
    end if
  end subroutine file_registry_write
    
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{39}Open a file: find the appropriate entry.  Create a new entry and add
to the list if necessary.  The list is extended at the beginning.
Return the I/O unit number for the records.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{40}\moddef{File registries: file registry: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: open => file_registry_open
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{41}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine file_registry_open (registry, file, unit)
    class(file_registry_t), intent(inout) :: registry
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: file
    integer, intent(out), optional :: unit
    type(file_entry_t), pointer :: entry
    entry => registry%first
    FIND_ENTRY: do while (associated (entry))
       if (entry%get_file () == file)  exit FIND_ENTRY
       entry => entry%next
    end do FIND_ENTRY
    if (.not. associated (entry)) then
       allocate (entry)
       call entry%init (file)
       if (associated (registry%first)) then
          registry%first%prev => entry
          entry%next => registry%first
       end if
       registry%first => entry
    end if
    call entry%open ()
    if (present (unit))  unit = entry%get_unit ()
  end subroutine file_registry_open

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{42}Close a file: find the appropriate entry.  Delete the entry if there
is no file connected to it anymore.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{43}\moddef{File registries: file registry: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: close => file_registry_close
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{44}\moddef{File registries: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine file_registry_close (registry, file)
    class(file_registry_t), intent(inout) :: registry
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: file
    type(file_entry_t), pointer :: entry
    entry => registry%first
    FIND_ENTRY: do while (associated (entry))
       if (entry%get_file () == file)  exit FIND_ENTRY
       entry => entry%next
    end do FIND_ENTRY
    if (associated (entry)) then
       call entry%close ()
       if (.not. entry%is_open ()) then
          if (associated (entry%prev)) then
             entry%prev%next => entry%next
          else
             registry%first => entry%next
          end if
          if (associated (entry%next)) then
             entry%next%prev => entry%prev
          end if
          deallocate (entry)
       end if
    end if
  end subroutine file_registry_close
    
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{45}\nwdocspar

\section{String Utilities}

This module provides tools associated with strings
(built-in and variable).  Currently:
\begin{itemize}
\item
  Upper and lower case for strings
\item
  Convert to null-terminated C string
\end{itemize}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{46}\moddef{\code{}string{\char95}utils.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module string_utils
  
  use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding
\LA{}Use kinds\RA{}  
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}String utils: public\RA{}

\LA{}String utils: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}String utils: procedures\RA{}

end module string_utils
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{47}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Upper and Lower Case}
These are, unfortunately, not part of Fortran.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{48}\moddef{String utils: public}\endmoddef
  public :: upper_case
  public :: lower_case
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{49}\moddef{String utils: interfaces}\endmoddef
  interface upper_case
     module procedure upper_case_char, upper_case_string
  end interface
  interface lower_case
     module procedure lower_case_char, lower_case_string
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{50}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\endmoddef
  function upper_case_char (string) result (new_string)
    character(*), intent(in) :: string
    character(len(string)) :: new_string
    integer :: pos, code
    integer, parameter :: offset = ichar('A')-ichar('a')
    do pos = 1, len (string)
       code = ichar (string(pos:pos))
       select case (code)
       case (ichar('a'):ichar('z'))
          new_string(pos:pos) = char (code + offset)
       case default
          new_string(pos:pos) = string(pos:pos)
       end select
    end do
  end function upper_case_char

  function lower_case_char (string) result (new_string)
    character(*), intent(in) :: string
    character(len(string)) :: new_string
    integer :: pos, code
    integer, parameter :: offset = ichar('a')-ichar('A')
    do pos = 1, len (string)
       code = ichar (string(pos:pos))
       select case (code)
       case (ichar('A'):ichar('Z'))
          new_string(pos:pos) = char (code + offset)
       case default
          new_string(pos:pos) = string(pos:pos)
       end select
    end do
  end function lower_case_char

  function upper_case_string (string) result (new_string)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    type(string_t) :: new_string
    new_string = upper_case_char (char (string))
  end function upper_case_string

  function lower_case_string (string) result (new_string)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    type(string_t) :: new_string
    new_string = lower_case_char (char (string))
  end function lower_case_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{51}\nwdocspar
\subsection{C-compatible Output}
Convert a FORTRAN string into a zero terminated C string.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{52}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: string_f2c
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{53}\moddef{String utils: interfaces}\plusendmoddef
  interface string_f2c
     module procedure string_f2c_char, string_f2c_var_str
  end interface string_f2c
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{54}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  pure function string_f2c_char (i) result (o)
    character(*), intent(in) :: i
    character(kind=c_char, len=len (i) + 1) :: o
    o = i // c_null_char
  end function string_f2c_char

  pure function string_f2c_var_str (i) result (o)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: i
    character(kind=c_char, len=len (i) + 1) :: o
    o = char (i) // c_null_char
  end function string_f2c_var_str

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{55}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Number Conversion}
Convert an integer to a string.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{56}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: integer_to_string
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{57}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function integer_to_string (x) result (str)
    integer, intent(in) :: x
    type(string_t) :: str
    character(5) :: buf
    write (buf, '(I5)') x
    str = var_str (trim (adjustl (buf)))
  end function integer_to_string

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{58}\nwdocspar
Create a string from a number.  We use fixed format for the reals
and variable format for integers.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{59}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: str
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{60}\moddef{String utils: interfaces}\plusendmoddef
  interface str
     module procedure str_int, str_real
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{61}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function str_int (i) result (s)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type(string_t) :: s
    character(32) :: buffer
    write (buffer, "(I0)")  i
    s = var_str (trim (buffer))
  end function str_int
  
  function str_real (x) result (s)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    type(string_t) :: s
    character(32) :: buffer
    write (buffer, "(ES17.10)")  x
    s = var_str (trim (adjustl (buffer)))
  end function str_real
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{62}Auxiliary: Read real, integer, string value.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{63}\moddef{String utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: read_rval
  public :: read_ival
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{64}\moddef{String utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function read_rval (s) result (rval)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: s
    real(default) :: rval
    character(80) :: buffer
    buffer = s
    read (buffer, *)  rval
  end function read_rval
    
  function read_ival (s) result (ival)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: s
    integer :: ival
    character(80) :: buffer
    buffer = s
    read (buffer, *)  ival
  end function read_ival
    
\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{67}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Line Output}
Write a separator line.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{68}\moddef{Format utils: public}\endmoddef
  public :: write_separator
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{69}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\endmoddef
  subroutine write_separator (u, mode)
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    integer, intent(in), optional :: mode
    integer :: m
    m = 1;  if (present (mode))  m = mode
    select case (m)
    case default
       write (u, "(A)")  repeat ("-", 72)
    case (1)
       write (u, "(A)")  repeat ("-", 72)
    case (2)
       write (u, "(A)")  repeat ("=", 72)
    end select
  end subroutine write_separator
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{70}\nwdocspar
Indent the line with given number of blanks.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{71}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: write_indent
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{72}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine write_indent (unit, indent)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    integer, intent(in), optional :: indent
    if (present (indent)) then
       write (unit, "(1x,A)", advance="no")  repeat ("  ", indent)
    end if
  end subroutine write_indent

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{73}\nwdocspar
\subsection{\TeX-compatible Output}
Quote underscore characters for use in \TeX\ output.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{74}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: quote_underscore
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{75}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function quote_underscore (string) result (quoted)
    type(string_t) :: quoted
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: string
    type(string_t) :: part
    type(string_t) :: buffer
    buffer = string
    quoted = ""
    do
      call split (part, buffer, "_")
      quoted = quoted // part
      if (buffer == "")  exit
      quoted = quoted // "\\_"
    end do
  end function quote_underscore

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{76}Format a number with $n$ significant digits for use in \TeX\ documents.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{77}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: tex_format
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{78}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function tex_format (rval, n_digits) result (string)
    type(string_t) :: string
    real(default), intent(in) :: rval
    integer, intent(in) :: n_digits
    integer :: e, n, w, d
    real(default) :: absval
    real(default) :: mantissa
    character :: sign
    character(20) :: format
    character(80) :: cstr
    n = min (abs (n_digits), 16)
    if (rval == 0) then
       string = "0"
    else
       absval = abs (rval)
       e = log10 (absval)
       if (rval < 0) then
          sign = "-"
       else
          sign = ""
       end if
       select case (e)
       case (:-3)
          d = max (n - 1, 0)
          w = max (d + 2, 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,',A,I0,A)')")  w, d
          mantissa = absval * 10._default ** (1 - e)
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  mantissa, "\\times 10^\{", e - 1, "\}"
       case (-2:0)
          d = max (n - e, 1 - e)
          w = max (d + e + 2, d + 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,')')")  w, d
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  absval
       case (1:2)
          d = max (n - e - 1, -e, 0)
          w = max (d + e + 2, d + 2, e + 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,')')")  w, d
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  absval
       case default
          d = max (n - 1, 0)
          w = max (d + 2, 2)
          write (format, "('(F',I0,'.',I0,',A,I0,A)')")  w, d
          mantissa = absval * 10._default ** (- e)
          write (cstr, fmt=format)  mantissa, "\\times 10^\{", e, "\}"
       end select
       string = sign // trim (cstr)
    end if
  end function tex_format

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{79}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Metapost-compatible Output}
Write a number for use in Metapost code:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{80}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: mp_format
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{81}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function mp_format (rval) result (string)
    type(string_t) :: string
    real(default), intent(in) :: rval
    character(16) :: tmp
    write (tmp, "(G16.8)")  rval
    string = lower_case (trim (adjustl (trim (tmp))))
  end function mp_format

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{82}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Conditional Formatting}
Conditional format string, intended for switchable numeric precision.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{83}\moddef{Format utils: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: pac_fmt
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{84}\moddef{Format utils: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine pac_fmt (fmt, fmt_orig, fmt_pac, pacify) 
    character(*), intent(in) :: fmt_orig, fmt_pac
    character(*), intent(out) :: fmt
    logical, intent(in), optional :: pacify
    logical :: pacified
    pacified = .false.
    if (present (pacify))  pacified = pacify
    if (pacified) then
       fmt = fmt_pac
    else
       fmt = fmt_orig
    end if
  end subroutine pac_fmt
  
\eatline

\chapter{Testing}
This part contains tools for automatic testing.
\begin{description}
\item[unit\_tests]
  A handler that executes test procedures and compares and collects results.
\end{description}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Unit tests}
We provide functionality for automated unit tests.  Each test is
required to produce output which is compared against a reference
file.  If the two are identical, we signal success.  Otherwise, we
signal failure and write the output to a file.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{2}\moddef{\code{}unit{\char95}tests.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module unit_tests

\LA{}Use kinds\RA{}
  use constants, only: zero, tiny_10, tiny_13
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: public\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: parameters\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: types\RA{}

\LA{}Tests: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Tests: procedures\RA{}

end module unit_tests
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{3}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Parameters}
Building blocks of file names.  The directory names and suffixes are
hard-coded here, and they must reflect actual Makefile targets where
applicable.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{4}\moddef{Tests: parameters}\endmoddef
  character(*), parameter :: ref_prefix = "ref-output/"
  character(*), parameter :: ref = ".ref"

  character(*), parameter :: err_prefix = "err-output/"
  character(*), parameter :: err = ".out"

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{5}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Type for storing test results}
We store the results of the individual unit tests in a linked list.
Here is the entry:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{6}\moddef{Tests: public}\endmoddef
  public :: test_results_t
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{7}\moddef{Tests: types}\endmoddef
  type :: test_result_t
     logical :: success = .false.
     type(string_t) :: name
     type(string_t) :: description
     type(test_result_t), pointer :: next => null ()
  end type test_result_t

  type :: test_results_t
     private
     type(test_result_t), pointer :: first => null ()
     type(test_result_t), pointer :: last => null ()
     integer :: n_success = 0
     integer :: n_failure = 0
   contains
   \LA{}Tests: test results: TBP\RA{}
  end type test_results_t

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{8}Add a test result.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{9}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\endmoddef
  procedure, private :: add => test_results_add
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{10}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\endmoddef
  subroutine test_results_add (list, name, description, success)
    class(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: list
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: name
    character(len=*), intent(in) :: description
    logical, intent(in) :: success
    type(test_result_t), pointer :: result
    allocate (result)
    result%success = success
    result%name = name
    result%description = description
    if (associated (list%first)) then
       list%last%next => result
    else
       list%first => result
    end if
    list%last => result
    if (success) then
       list%n_success = list%n_success + 1
    else
       list%n_failure = list%n_failure + 1
    end if
  end subroutine test_results_add

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{11}Display the current state.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{12}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure, private :: write => test_results_write
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{13}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine test_results_write (list, u)
    class(test_results_t), intent(in) :: list
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    type(test_result_t), pointer :: result
    write (u, "(A)")  "*** Test Summary ***"
    if (list%n_success > 0) then
       write (u, "(2x,A)")  "Success:"
       result => list%first
       do while (associated (result))
          if (result%success)  write (u, "(4x,A,': ',A)")  &
               char (result%name), char (result%description)
          result => result%next
       end do
    end if
    if (list%n_failure > 0) then
       write (u, "(2x,A)")  "Failure:"
       result => list%first
       do while (associated (result))
          if (.not. result%success)  write (u, "(4x,A,': ',A)")  &
               char (result%name), char (result%description)
          result => result%next
       end do
    end if
    write (u, "(A,I0)")  "Total   = ", list%n_success + list%n_failure
    write (u, "(A,I0)")  "Success = ", list%n_success
    write (u, "(A,I0)")  "Failure = ", list%n_failure
    write (u, "(A)")  "*** End of test Summary ***"
  end subroutine test_results_write

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{14}Return true if all tests were successful (or no test).
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{15}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure, private :: report => test_results_report
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{16}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine test_results_report (list, success)
    class(test_results_t), intent(in) :: list
    logical, intent(out) :: success
    success = list%n_failure == 0
  end subroutine test_results_report

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{17}Delete the list.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{18}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure, private :: final => test_results_final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{19}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine test_results_final (list)
    class(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: list
    type(test_result_t), pointer :: result
    do while (associated (list%first))
       result => list%first
       list%first => result%next
       deallocate (result)
    end do
    list%last => null ()
    list%n_success = 0
    list%n_failure = 0
  end subroutine test_results_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{20}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Wrapup}
This will write results, report status, and finalize.  This is the
only method which we need to access from outside.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{21}\moddef{Tests: test results: TBP}\plusendmoddef
  procedure :: wrapup => test_results_wrapup
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{22}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine test_results_wrapup (list, u, success)
    class(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: list
    integer, intent(in) :: u
    logical, intent(out), optional :: success
    call list%write (u)
    if (present (success))  call list%report (success)
    call list%final ()
  end subroutine test_results_wrapup

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{23}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Tool for Unit Tests}
This procedure takes a test routine as an argument.  It runs the test,
output directed to a temporary file.  Then, it compares the file
against a reference file.

The test routine must take the output unit as argument.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{24}\moddef{Tests: interfaces}\endmoddef
  abstract interface
     subroutine unit_test (u)
       integer, intent(in) :: u
     end subroutine unit_test
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{25}The test routine can print to screen and, optionally, to a logging unit.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{26}\moddef{Tests: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: test
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{27}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine test (test_proc, name, description, u_log, results)
    procedure(unit_test) :: test_proc
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    character(*), intent(in) :: description
    integer, intent(in) :: u_log
    type(test_results_t), intent(inout) :: results
    integer :: u_test, u_ref, u_err
    logical :: exist
    character(256) :: buffer1, buffer2
    integer :: iostat1, iostat2
    logical :: success
    write (*, "(A)", advance="no")  "Running test: " // name
    write (u_log, "(A)")  "Test: " // name
    u_test = free_unit ()
    open (u_test, status="scratch", action="readwrite")
    call test_proc (u_test)
    rewind (u_test)
    inquire (file=ref_prefix//name//ref, exist=exist)
    if (exist) then
       u_ref = free_unit ()
       open (u_ref, file=ref_prefix//name//ref, status="old", action="read")
       COMPARE_FILES: do
          read (u_test, "(A)", iostat=iostat1)  buffer1
          read (u_ref, "(A)", iostat=iostat2)  buffer2
          if (iostat1 /= iostat2) then
             success = .false.
             exit COMPARE_FILES
          else if (iostat1 < 0) then
             success = .true.
             exit COMPARE_FILES
          else if (buffer1 /= buffer2) then
             success = .false.
             exit COMPARE_FILES
          end if
       end do COMPARE_FILES
       close (u_ref)
    else
       write (*, "(A)", advance="no") " ... no reference output available"
       write (u_log, "(A)") "  No reference output available."
       success = .false.
    end if
    if (success) then
       write (*, "(A)") " ... success."
       write (u_log, "(A)")  "  Success."
    else
       write (*, "(A)") " ... failure.  See: " // err_prefix//name//err
       write (u_log, "(A)")  "  Failure."
       rewind (u_test)
       u_err = free_unit ()
       open (u_err, file=err_prefix//name//err, &
            action="write", status="replace")
       WRITE_OUTPUT: do
          read (u_test, "(A)", end=1) buffer1
          write (u_err, "(A)")  trim (buffer1)
       end do WRITE_OUTPUT
1      close (u_err)
    end if
    close (u_test)
    call results%add (name, description, success)
  end subroutine test

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{28}\subsection{Convenience functions}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegindocs{29}Unit tests should include a lot of assertions that only involve IO if
something is wrong. {\tt{}assert} allows to streamline this method.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{30}\moddef{Tests: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: assert
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{31}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine assert (unit, ok, description)
    integer, intent(in) :: unit
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: description
    if (.not. ok) then
       if (present(description)) then
          write (unit, "(A)") "* FAIL: " // description
       else
          write (unit, "(A)") "* FAIL: Assertion error"
       end if
    end if
  end subroutine assert

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{32}Note that this poor man's check will be disabled if someone compiles
with {\tt{}-ffast-math} or similar optimizations.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{33}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  elemental function ieee_is_nan (x) result (yorn)
    logical :: yorn
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    yorn = (x /= x)
  end function ieee_is_nan
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{34}This is still not perfect but should work in most cases.  Usually one
wants to compare to a relative epsilon {\tt{}rel{\char95}smallness}, except for
numbers close to zero defined by {\tt{}abs{\char95}smallness}.  Both might need
adaption to specific use cases but have reasonable defaults.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{35}\moddef{Tests: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: nearly_equal
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{36}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  elemental function nearly_equal (a, b, abs_smallness, rel_smallness) result (r)
    logical :: r
    real(default), intent(in) :: a, b
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    real(default) :: abs_a, abs_b, diff, abs_small, rel_small
    abs_a = abs (a)
    abs_b = abs (b)
    diff = abs (a - b)
    ! shortcut, handles infinities and nans
    if (a == b) then
       r = .true.
       return
    else if (ieee_is_nan (a) .or. ieee_is_nan (b) .or. ieee_is_nan (diff)) then
       r = .false.
       return
    end if
    if (present (abs_smallness)) then
       abs_small = abs_smallness
    else
       abs_small = tiny_13
    end if
    if (present (rel_smallness)) then
       rel_small = rel_smallness
    else
       rel_small = tiny_10
    end if
    if (abs_a < abs_small .and. abs_b < abs_small) then
       r = diff < abs_small
    else
       r = diff / max (abs_a, abs_b) < rel_small
    end if
  end function nearly_equal

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{37}Often we will need to check whether floats vanish:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{38}\moddef{Tests: public}\plusendmoddef
  public:: vanishes
  interface vanishes
     module procedure vanishes_real, vanishes_complex
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{39}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{40}\moddef{Tests: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  elemental function vanishes_real (x, abs_smallness, rel_smallness) result (r)
    logical :: r
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    r = nearly_equal (x, zero, abs_smallness, rel_smallness)
  end function vanishes_real

  elemental function vanishes_complex (x, abs_smallness, rel_smallness) result (r)
    logical :: r
    complex(default), intent(in) :: x
    real(default), intent(in), optional :: abs_smallness, rel_smallness
    r = vanishes_real (abs (x), abs_smallness, rel_smallness)
  end function vanishes_complex

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{41}\nwdocspar

\nwenddocs{}\nwbegindocs{1}\nwdocspar
\chapter{System: Interfaces and Handlers}
Here, we collect modules that deal with the ``system'':
operating-system interfaces, error handlers and diagnostics.
\begin{description}
\item[system\_defs] 
  Constants relevant for the modules in this set.
\item[diagnostics] 
  Error and diagnostic message handling.  Any
  messages and errors issued by WHIZARD functions are handled by the
  subroutines in this module, if possible.
\item[os\_interface] 
  Execute system calls, build and link external object files and libraries.
\item[cputime]
  Timer data type and methods, for measuring performance.
\end{description}

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Constants}
The parameters here are used in various parts of the program,
starting from the modules in the current chapter.  Some of them may be
modified if the need arises.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{2}\moddef{\code{}system{\char95}defs.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module system_defs

  use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: iostat_end, iostat_eor !NODEP!

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}System defs: public parameters\RA{}

end module system_defs
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{3}\nwdocspar

The version string is used for checking files.  Note that the string
length MUST NOT be changed, because reading binary files relies on it.

  character(len=VERSION_STRLEN), parameter, public :: &
       & VERSION_STRING = "WHIZARD version \LA{}Version\RA{} (\LA{}Date\RA{})"

\eatline

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{13}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{C wrapper for sigaction}
This implements calls to {\tt{}sigaction} and the appropriate signal handlers in
C.  The functionality is needed for the {\tt{}diagnostics} module.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{14}\moddef{\code{}signal{\char95}interface.c\edoc{}}\endmoddef
/*
\LA{}File header\RA{}
*/
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

extern int wo_sigint;
extern int wo_sigterm;
extern int wo_sigxcpu;
extern int wo_sigxfsz;

static void wo_handler_sigint (int sig) \{
  wo_sigint = sig;
\}

static void wo_handler_sigterm (int sig) \{
  wo_sigterm = sig;
\}

static void wo_handler_sigxcpu (int sig) \{
  wo_sigxcpu = sig;
\}

static void wo_handler_sigxfsz (int sig) \{
  wo_sigxfsz = sig;
\}

int wo_mask_sigint () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigint;
  return sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_mask_sigterm () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigterm;
  return sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_mask_sigxcpu () \{
  struct sigaction sa;  
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigxcpu;
  return sigaction(SIGXCPU, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_mask_sigxfsz () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = wo_handler_sigxfsz;
  return sigaction(SIGXFSZ, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigint () \{
  struct sigaction sa;  
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigterm () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigxcpu () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGXCPU, &sa, NULL);
\}

int wo_release_sigxfsz () \{
  struct sigaction sa;
  sigset_t blocks;
  sigfillset (&blocks);
  sa.sa_flags = 0;
  sa.sa_mask = blocks;
  sa.sa_handler = SIG_DFL;
  return sigaction(SIGXFSZ, &sa, NULL);
\}
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{15}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{C wrapper for printf}
The {\tt{}printf} family of functions is implemented in C with an undefined
number of arguments.  This is not supported by the {\tt{}bind(C)} interface.  We
therefore write wrappers for the versions of {\tt{}sprintf} that
we will actually use.

This is used by the {\tt{}formats} module.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{16}\moddef{\code{}sprintf{\char95}interface.c\edoc{}}\endmoddef
/*
\LA{}File header\RA{}
*/
#include <stdio.h>

int sprintf_none(char* str, const char* format) \{
  return sprintf(str, format);
\}

int sprintf_int(char* str, const char* format, int val) \{
  return sprintf(str, format, val);
\}

int sprintf_double(char* str, const char* format, double val) \{
  return sprintf(str, format, val);
\}

int sprintf_str(char* str, const char* format, const char* val) \{
  return sprintf(str, format, val);
\}

\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{17}\moddef{sprintf interfaces}\endmoddef
  interface
    function sprintf_none (str, fmt) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
    end function sprintf_none
  end interface
      
  interface
    function sprintf_int (str, fmt, val) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
      integer(c_int), value :: val
    end function sprintf_int
  end interface
      
  interface
    function sprintf_double (str, fmt, val) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
      real(c_double), value :: val
    end function sprintf_double
  end interface
      
  interface
    function sprintf_str(str, fmt, val) result (stat) bind(C)
      use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
      integer(c_int) :: stat
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(inout) :: str
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: fmt
      character(c_char), dimension(*), intent(in) :: val
    end function sprintf_str
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{18}\nwdocspar
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Error, Message and Signal Handling}
We are not so ambitious as to do proper exception handling in
{\tt{}WHIZARD}, but at least it may be useful to have a common interface
for diagnostics: Results, messages, warnings, and such.  As module
variables we keep a buffer where the current message may be written to
and a level indicator which tells which messages should be written on
screen and which ones should be skipped.  Alternatively, a string may
be directly supplied to the message routine: this overrides the
buffer, avoiding the necessety of formatted I/O in trivial cases.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{19}\moddef{\code{}diagnostics.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef
\LA{}File header\RA{}

module diagnostics

  use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding !NODEP! 
  use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: output_unit !NODEP!

\LA{}Use kinds\RA{}
\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units

  use system_dependencies
  use system_defs, only: BUFFER_SIZE, MAX_ERRORS

\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: public\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: parameters\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: types\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: variables\RA{}

\LA{}Diagnostics: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}Diagnostics: procedures\RA{}

end module diagnostics
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{20}\nwdocspar
Diagnostics levels:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{21}\moddef{Diagnostics: parameters}\endmoddef
  integer, parameter :: &
       & TERMINATE=-2, BUG=-1, &
       & FATAL=1, ERROR=2, WARNING=3, MESSAGE=4, RESULT=5, DEBUG=6
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{22}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\endmoddef
  integer, save :: msg_level = RESULT
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{23}\nwdocspar
Mask fatal errors so that are treated as normal errors.  Useful for
interactive mode.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{24}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\endmoddef
  public :: mask_fatal_errors
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{25}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  logical, save :: mask_fatal_errors = .false.
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{26}\nwdocspar
How to handle bugs and unmasked fatal errors.  Either execute a normal
stop statement, or call the C {\tt{}exit()} function, or try to cause a
program crash by dereferencing a null pointer.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{27}\moddef{Diagnostics: parameters}\plusendmoddef
  integer, parameter :: TERM_STOP = 0, TERM_EXIT = 1, TERM_CRASH = 2
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{28}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  integer, save :: handle_fatal_errors = TERM_EXIT
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{29}\nwdocspar
Keep track of errors.  This might be used for exception handling,
later.  The counter is incremented only for screen messages, to avoid
double counting.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{30}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: msg_count
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{31}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  integer, dimension(TERMINATE:DEBUG), save :: msg_count = 0
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{32}Keep a list of all errors and warnings.  Since we do not know the number of
entries beforehand, we use a linked list.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{33}\moddef{Diagnostics: types}\endmoddef
  type :: string_list
     character(len=BUFFER_SIZE) :: string
     type(string_list), pointer :: next
  end type string_list
  type :: string_list_pointer
     type(string_list), pointer :: first, last
  end type string_list_pointer
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{34}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  type(string_list_pointer), dimension(TERMINATE:WARNING), save :: &
       & msg_list = string_list_pointer (null(), null())
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{35}Add the current message buffer contents to the internal list.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{36}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\endmoddef
  subroutine msg_add (level)
    integer, intent(in) :: level
    type(string_list), pointer :: message
    select case (level)
    case (TERMINATE:WARNING)
       allocate (message)
       message%string = msg_buffer
       nullify (message%next)
       if (.not.associated (msg_list(level)%first)) &
            & msg_list(level)%first => message
       if (associated (msg_list(level)%last)) &
            & msg_list(level)%last%next => message
       msg_list(level)%last => message
       msg_count(level) = msg_count(level) + 1
    end select
  end subroutine msg_add

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{37}\nwdocspar
Initialization: 
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{38}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: msg_list_clear
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{39}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine msg_list_clear
    integer :: level
    type(string_list), pointer :: message
    do level = TERMINATE, WARNING
       do while (associated (msg_list(level)%first))
          message => msg_list(level)%first
          msg_list(level)%first => message%next
          deallocate (message)
       end do
       nullify (msg_list(level)%last)
    end do
    msg_count = 0
  end subroutine msg_list_clear

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{40}Display the summary of errors and warnings (no need to count
fatals\ldots)
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{41}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: msg_summary
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{42}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine msg_summary (unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    call expect_summary (unit)
1   format (A,1x,I2,1x,A,I2,1x,A)
    if (msg_count(ERROR) > 0 .and. msg_count(WARNING) > 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, 1) "There were", &
            & msg_count(ERROR), "error(s) and  ", &
            & msg_count(WARNING), "warning(s)."
       call msg_message (unit=unit)
    else if (msg_count(ERROR) > 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, 1) "There were", &
            & msg_count(ERROR), "error(s) and no warnings."
       call msg_message (unit=unit)
    else if (msg_count(WARNING) > 0) then
       write (msg_buffer, 1) "There were no errors and  ", &
            & msg_count(WARNING), "warning(s)."
       call msg_message (unit=unit)
    end if
  end subroutine msg_summary

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{43}Print the list of all messages of a given level.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{44}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: msg_listing
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{45}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine msg_listing (level, unit, prefix)
    integer, intent(in) :: level
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: prefix
    type(string_list), pointer :: message
    integer :: u
    u = given_output_unit (unit);  if (u < 0)  return
    if (present (unit))  u = unit
    message => msg_list(level)%first
    do while (associated (message))
       if (present (prefix)) then
          write (u, "(A)") prefix // trim (message%string)
       else
          write (u, "(A)") trim (message%string)
       end if
       message => message%next
    end do
    flush (u)
  end subroutine msg_listing

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{46}The message buffer:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{47}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: msg_buffer
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{48}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  character(len=BUFFER_SIZE), save :: msg_buffer = " "
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{49}\nwdocspar
After a message is issued, the buffer should be cleared:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{50}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine buffer_clear
    msg_buffer = " "
  end subroutine buffer_clear

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{51}The generic handler for messages.  If the unit is omitted (or $=6$), the
message is written to standard output if the precedence if
sufficiently high (as determined by the value of
{\tt{}msg{\char95}level}).  If the string is omitted, the buffer is used.
In any case, the buffer is cleared after printing.  In accordance with
FORTRAN custom, the first column in the output is left blank.  For
messages and warnings, an additional exclamation mark and a blank is
prepended.  Furthermore, each message is appended to the internal
message list (without prepending anything).
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{52}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine message_print (level, string, str_arr, unit, logfile)
    integer, intent(in) :: level
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: str_arr
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: logfile   
    type(string_t) :: prep_string, aux_string, head_footer
    integer :: lu, i
    logical :: severe, is_error
    severe = .false.
    head_footer  = "******************************************************************************"
    aux_string = ""
    is_error = .false.
    select case (level)
    case (TERMINATE)
       prep_string = ""
    case (BUG)
       prep_string   = "*** WHIZARD BUG: "
       aux_string    = "***              "
       severe = .true.
       is_error = .true.
    case (FATAL)
       prep_string   = "*** FATAL ERROR: "
       aux_string    = "***              "                     
       severe = .true.
       is_error = .true.
    case (ERROR)
       prep_string = "*** ERROR: "
       aux_string  = "***        "
       is_error = .true.
    case (WARNING)
       prep_string = "Warning: "
    case (MESSAGE, DEBUG)
       prep_string = "| "
    case default
       prep_string = ""
    end select
    if (present(string))  msg_buffer = string
    lu = log_unit
    if (present(unit)) then
       if (unit /= output_unit) then
          if (severe) write (unit, "(A)") char(head_footer) 
          if (is_error) write (unit, "(A)") char(head_footer) 
          write (unit, "(A,A)") char(prep_string), trim(msg_buffer)
          if (present (str_arr)) then
             do i = 1, size(str_arr)
                write (unit, "(A,A)") char(aux_string), char(trim(str_arr(i)))
             end do
          end if
          if (is_error) write (unit, "(A)") char(head_footer) 
          if (severe) write (unit, "(A)") char(head_footer)
          flush (unit)
          lu = -1
       else if (level <= msg_level) then
          if (severe) print "(A)", char(head_footer) 
          if (is_error) print "(A)", char(head_footer) 
          print "(A,A)", char(prep_string), trim(msg_buffer)
          if (present (str_arr)) then
             do i = 1, size(str_arr)
                print "(A,A)", char(aux_string), char(trim(str_arr(i)))
             end do                
          end if
          if (is_error) print "(A)", char(head_footer) 
          if (severe) print "(A)", char(head_footer)
          flush (output_unit)
          if (unit == log_unit)  lu = -1
       end if
    else if (level <= msg_level) then
       if (severe) print "(A)", char(head_footer) 
       if (is_error) print "(A)", char(head_footer) 
       print "(A,A)", char(prep_string), trim(msg_buffer)
          if (present (str_arr)) then
             do i = 1, size(str_arr)
                print "(A,A)", char(aux_string), char(trim(str_arr(i)))
             end do                
          end if
       if (is_error) print "(A)", char(head_footer) 
       if (severe) print "(A)", char(head_footer) 
       flush (output_unit)
    end if
    if (present (logfile)) then
       if (.not. logfile)  lu = -1
    end if
    if (logging .and. lu >= 0) then
       if (severe) write (lu, "(A)") char(head_footer) 
       if (is_error) write (lu, "(A)") char(head_footer) 
       write (lu, "(A,A)")  char(prep_string), trim(msg_buffer)
       if (present (str_arr)) then
          do i = 1, size(str_arr)
             write (lu, "(A,A)") char(aux_string), char(trim(str_arr(i)))
          end do                
       end if
       if (is_error) write (lu, "(A)") char(head_footer) 
       if (severe) write (lu, "(A)") char(head_footer) 
       flush (lu)
    end if
    call msg_add (level)
    call buffer_clear
  end subroutine message_print

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{53}\nwdocspar
The number of non-fatal errors that we allow before stopping the
program.  We might trade this later for an adjustable number.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{54}\moddef{System defs: public parameters}\plusendmoddef
  integer, parameter, public :: MAX_ERRORS = 10
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{55}The specific handlers.  In the case of fatal errors, bugs (failed
assertions) and normal termination execution is stopped.  For
non-fatal errors a message is printed to standard output if no unit is
given.  Only if the number of {\tt{}MAX{\char95}ERRORS} errors is reached, we
abort the program.  There are no further actions in the other cases,
but this may change.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{56}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: msg_terminate
  public :: msg_bug, msg_fatal, msg_error, msg_warning
  public :: msg_message, msg_result, msg_debug
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{57}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine msg_terminate (string, unit, quit_code)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    integer, intent(in), optional :: quit_code
    integer(c_int) :: return_code
    call release_term_signals ()
    if (present (quit_code)) then
       return_code = quit_code
    else
       return_code = 0
    end if
    if (present (string)) &
         call message_print (MESSAGE, string, unit=unit)
    call msg_summary (unit)
    if (return_code == 0 .and. expect_failures /= 0) then
       return_code = 5
       call message_print (MESSAGE, &
            "WHIZARD run finished with 'expect' failure(s).", unit=unit)
    else if (return_code == 7) then
       call message_print (MESSAGE, &
            "WHIZARD run finished with failed self-test.", unit=unit)
    else
       call message_print (MESSAGE, "WHIZARD run finished.", unit=unit)
    end if
    call message_print (0, &
         "|=============================================================================|", unit=unit)
    call logfile_final ()
    call msg_list_clear ()
    if (return_code /= 0) then
       call exit (return_code)
    else 
       !!! Should implement WHIZARD exit code (currently only via C)
       ! stop
       call exit (0)
    end if
  end subroutine msg_terminate

  subroutine msg_bug (string, arr, unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: arr
    logical, pointer :: crash_ptr
    call message_print (BUG, string, arr, unit)
    call msg_summary (unit)
    select case (handle_fatal_errors)
    case (TERM_EXIT)
       call message_print (TERMINATE, "WHIZARD run aborted.", unit=unit)
       call exit (-1_c_int)
    case (TERM_CRASH)
       print *, "*** Intentional crash ***"
       crash_ptr => null ()
       print *, crash_ptr
    end select
    stop "WHIZARD run aborted."
  end subroutine msg_bug

  recursive subroutine msg_fatal (string, arr, unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: arr
    logical, pointer :: crash_ptr
    if (mask_fatal_errors) then
       call msg_error (string, arr, unit)
    else
       call message_print (FATAL, string, arr, unit)
       call msg_summary (unit)
       select case (handle_fatal_errors)
       case (TERM_EXIT)
          call message_print (TERMINATE, "WHIZARD run aborted.", unit=unit)
          call exit (1_c_int)
       case (TERM_CRASH)
          print *, "*** Intentional crash ***"
          crash_ptr => null ()
          print *, crash_ptr
       end select
       stop "WHIZARD run aborted."
    end if
  end subroutine msg_fatal

  subroutine msg_error (string, arr, unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: arr
    call message_print (ERROR, string, arr, unit)
    if (msg_count(ERROR) >= MAX_ERRORS) then
       mask_fatal_errors = .false.
       call msg_fatal (" Too many errors encountered.")
    else if (.not.present(unit) .and. .not.mask_fatal_errors)  then
       call message_print (MESSAGE, "            (WHIZARD run continues)")
    end if
  end subroutine msg_error

  subroutine msg_warning (string, arr, unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: arr
    call message_print (WARNING, string, arr, unit)
  end subroutine msg_warning

  subroutine msg_message (string, unit, arr, logfile)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: arr
    logical, intent(in), optional :: logfile
    call message_print (MESSAGE, string, arr, unit, logfile)
  end subroutine msg_message

  subroutine msg_result (string, arr, unit, logfile)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: arr
    logical, intent(in), optional :: logfile
    call message_print (RESULT, string, arr, unit, logfile)
  end subroutine msg_result

  subroutine msg_debug (string, arr, unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    character(len=*), intent(in), optional :: string
    type(string_t), dimension(:), intent(in), optional :: arr
    call message_print (DEBUG, string, arr, unit)
  end subroutine msg_debug

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{58}Interface to the standard clib exit function
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{59}\moddef{Diagnostics: interfaces}\endmoddef
  interface
     subroutine exit (status) bind (C)
       use iso_c_binding !NODEP!
       integer(c_int), value :: status
     end subroutine exit
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{60}Print the WHIZARD banner:
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{61}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: msg_banner
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{62}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine msg_banner (unit)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    integer :: n_proc
    call message_print (0, "|=============================================================================|", unit=unit)
    call message_print (0, "|                                                                             |", unit=unit)
    call message_print (0, "|    WW             WW  WW   WW  WW  WWWWWW      WW      WWWWW    WWWW        |", unit=unit)
    call message_print (0, "|     WW    WW     WW   WW   WW  WW     WW      WWWW     WW  WW   WW  WW      |", unit=unit)
    call message_print (0, "|      WW  WW WW  WW    WWWWWWW  WW    WW      WW  WW    WWWWW    WW   WW     |", unit=unit)
    call message_print (0, "|       WWWW   WWWW     WW   WW  WW   WW      WWWWWWWW   WW  WW   WW  WW      |", unit=unit)
    call message_print (0, "|        WW     WW      WW   WW  WW  WWWWWW  WW      WW  WW   WW  WWWW        |", unit=unit)
    call message_print (0, "|                                                                             |", unit=unit)

\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{63}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Logfile}
All screen output should be duplicated in the logfile, unless
requested otherwise.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{64}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: logging
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{65}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  integer, save :: log_unit = -1
  logical, target, save :: logging = .false.
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{66}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: logfile_init
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{67}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine logfile_init (filename)
    type(string_t), intent(in) :: filename
    call msg_message ("Writing log to '" // char (filename) // "'")
    if (.not. logging)  call msg_message ("(Logging turned off.)")
    log_unit = free_unit ()
    open (file = char (filename), unit = log_unit, &
          action = "write", status = "replace")
  end subroutine logfile_init

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{68}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: logfile_final
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{69}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine logfile_final ()
    if (log_unit >= 0) then
       close (log_unit)
       log_unit = -1
    end if
  end subroutine logfile_final

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{70}This returns the valid logfile unit only if the default is write to
screen, and if {\tt{}logfile} is not set false.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{71}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: logfile_unit
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{72}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function logfile_unit (unit, logfile)
    integer :: logfile_unit
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: logfile
    if (logging) then
       if (present (unit)) then
          if (unit == output_unit) then
             logfile_unit = log_unit
          else
             logfile_unit = -1
          end if
       else if (present (logfile)) then
          if (logfile) then
             logfile_unit = log_unit
          else
             logfile_unit = -1
          end if
       else
          logfile_unit = log_unit
       end if
    else
       logfile_unit = -1
    end if
  end function logfile_unit

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{73}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Checking values}
The {\tt{}expect} function does not just check a value for correctness
(actually, it checks if a logical expression is true); it records its
result here.  If failures are present when the program terminates, the
exit code is nonzero.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{74}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  integer, save :: expect_total = 0
  integer, save :: expect_failures = 0

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{75}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: expect_record
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{76}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine expect_record (success)
    logical, intent(in) :: success
    expect_total = expect_total + 1
    if (.not. success)  expect_failures = expect_failures + 1
  end subroutine expect_record

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{77}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: expect_clear
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{78}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine expect_clear ()
    expect_total = 0
    expect_failures = 0
  end subroutine expect_clear

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{79}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: expect_summary
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{80}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine expect_summary (unit, force)
    integer, intent(in), optional :: unit
    logical, intent(in), optional :: force
    logical :: force_output
    force_output = .false.;  if (present (force))  force_output = force
    if (expect_total /= 0 .or. force_output) then
       call msg_message ("Summary of value checks:", unit)
       write (msg_buffer, "(2x,A,1x,I0,1x,A,1x,A,1x,I0)") &
            "Failures:", expect_failures, "/", "Total:", expect_total
       call msg_message (unit=unit)
    end if
  end subroutine expect_summary

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{81}Helpers for converting integers into strings with minimal length.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{82}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: int2string
  public :: int2char
  public :: int2fixed
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{83}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  pure function int2fixed (i) result (c)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    character(200) :: c
    c = ""
    write (c, *) i
    c = adjustl (c)
  end function int2fixed

  pure function int2string (i) result (s)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    type (string_t) :: s
    s = trim (int2fixed (i))
  end function int2string

  pure function int2char (i) result (c)
    integer, intent(in) :: i
    character(len (trim (int2fixed (i)))) :: c
    c = int2fixed (i)
  end function int2char

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{84}Dito for reals.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{85}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: real2string
  public :: real2char
  public :: real2fixed
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{86}\moddef{Diagnostics: interfaces}\plusendmoddef
  interface real2string
     module procedure real2string_list, real2string_fmt
  end interface
  interface real2char
     module procedure real2char_list, real2char_fmt
  end interface
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{87}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  pure function real2fixed (x, fmt) result (c)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    character(*), intent(in), optional :: fmt
    character(200) :: c
    c = ""
    write (c, *) x
    c = adjustl (c)
  end function real2fixed

  pure function real2fixed_fmt (x, fmt) result (c)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    character(*), intent(in) :: fmt
    character(200) :: c
    c = ""
    write (c, fmt)  x
    c = adjustl (c)
  end function real2fixed_fmt

  pure function real2string_list (x) result (s)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    type(string_t) :: s
    s = trim (real2fixed (x))
  end function real2string_list

  pure function real2string_fmt (x, fmt) result (s)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    character(*), intent(in) :: fmt
    type(string_t) :: s
    s = trim (real2fixed_fmt (x, fmt))
  end function real2string_fmt

  pure function real2char_list (x) result (c)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    character(len_trim (real2fixed (x))) :: c
    c = real2fixed (x)
  end function real2char_list

  pure function real2char_fmt (x, fmt) result (c)
    real(default), intent(in) :: x
    character(*), intent(in) :: fmt
    character(len_trim (real2fixed_fmt (x, fmt))) :: c
    c = real2fixed_fmt (x, fmt)
  end function real2char_fmt

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{88}Dito for complex values; we do not use the slightly ugly FORTRAN output form
here but instead introduce our own. Ifort and Portland seem to have problems 
with this, therefore temporarily disable it.   
%
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{89}\moddef{CCC Diagnostics: public}\endmoddef
   public :: cmplx2string
   public :: cmplx2char
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{90}\moddef{CCC Diagnostics: procedures}\endmoddef
   pure function cmplx2string (x) result (s)
     complex(default), intent(in) :: x
     type(string_t) :: s
     s = real2string (real (x, default))
     if (aimag (x) /= 0) s = s // " + " // real2string (aimag (x)) // " I"
   end function cmplx2string

   pure function cmplx2char (x) result (c)
     complex(default), intent(in) :: x
     character(len (char (cmplx2string (x)))) :: c
     c = char (cmplx2string (x))
   end function cmplx2char
   
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{91}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Suppression of numerical noise}
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{92}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: pacify
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{93}\moddef{Diagnostics: interfaces}\plusendmoddef
  interface pacify
     module procedure pacify_real_default
     module procedure pacify_complex_default
  end interface pacify
  
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{94}\nwdocspar
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{95}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  elemental subroutine pacify_real_default (x, tolerance)
    real(default), intent(inout) :: x
    real(default), intent(in) :: tolerance
    if (abs (x) < tolerance)  x = 0
  end subroutine pacify_real_default
  
  elemental subroutine pacify_complex_default (x, tolerance)
    complex(default), intent(inout) :: x
    real(default), intent(in) :: tolerance
    if (abs (real (x)) < tolerance)   &
         x = cmplx (0._default, aimag (x), kind=default)
    if (abs (aimag (x)) < tolerance)  &
         x = cmplx (real (x), 0._default, kind=default)
  end subroutine pacify_complex_default  

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{96}\nwdocspar
\subsection{Signal handling}
Killing the program by external signals may leave the files written by it in
an undefined state.  This can be avoided by catching signals and deferring
program termination.  Instead of masking only critical sections, we choose
to mask signals globally (done in the main program) and terminate the program
at predefined checkpoints only.  Checkpoints are after each command, within
the sampling function (so the program can be terminated after each event),
and after each iteration in the phase-space generation algorithm.

Signal handling is done via a C interface to the {\tt{}sigaction} system call.
When a signal is raised that has been masked by the handler, the corresponding
variable is set to the value of the signal.  The variables are visible from
the C signal handler.

The signal SIGINT is for keyboard interrupt (ctrl-C), SIGTERM is for system
interrupt, e.g., at shutdown.  The SIGXCPU and SIGXFSZ signals may be issued
by batch systems.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{97}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: wo_sigint
  public :: wo_sigterm
  public :: wo_sigxcpu
  public :: wo_sigxfsz

\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{98}\moddef{Diagnostics: variables}\plusendmoddef
  integer(c_int), bind(C), volatile :: wo_sigint = 0
  integer(c_int), bind(C), volatile :: wo_sigterm = 0
  integer(c_int), bind(C), volatile :: wo_sigxcpu = 0
  integer(c_int), bind(C), volatile :: wo_sigxfsz = 0

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegindocs{99}Here are the interfaces to the C functions.  The routine
{\tt{}mask{\char95}term{\char95}signals} forces termination signals to be delayed.
{\tt{}release{\char95}term{\char95}signals} restores normal behavior.  However, the program can be
terminated anytime by calling {\tt{}terminate{\char95}now{\char95}if{\char95}signal} which inspects the
signals and terminates the program if requested..
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{100}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: mask_term_signals
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{101}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine mask_term_signals ()
    integer(c_int) :: status
    logical :: ok
    wo_sigint = 0
    ok = wo_mask_sigint () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Masking SIGINT failed")
    wo_sigterm = 0
    ok = wo_mask_sigterm () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Masking SIGTERM failed")
    wo_sigxcpu = 0
    ok = wo_mask_sigxcpu () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Masking SIGXCPU failed")
    wo_sigxfsz = 0
    ok = wo_mask_sigxfsz () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Masking SIGXFSZ failed")
  end subroutine mask_term_signals

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{102}\moddef{Diagnostics: interfaces}\plusendmoddef
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_mask_sigint () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_mask_sigint
  end interface
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_mask_sigterm () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_mask_sigterm
  end interface
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_mask_sigxcpu () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_mask_sigxcpu
  end interface
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_mask_sigxfsz () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_mask_sigxfsz
  end interface

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{103}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: release_term_signals
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{104}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine release_term_signals ()
    integer(c_int) :: status
    logical :: ok
    ok = wo_release_sigint () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Releasing SIGINT failed")
    ok = wo_release_sigterm () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Releasing SIGTERM failed")
    ok = wo_release_sigxcpu () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Releasing SIGXCPU failed")
    ok = wo_release_sigxfsz () == 0
    if (.not. ok)  call msg_error ("Releasing SIGXFSZ failed")
  end subroutine release_term_signals

\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{105}\moddef{Diagnostics: interfaces}\plusendmoddef
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_release_sigint () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_release_sigint
  end interface
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_release_sigterm () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_release_sigterm
  end interface
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_release_sigxcpu () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_release_sigxcpu
  end interface
  interface
     integer(c_int) function wo_release_sigxfsz () bind(C)
       import
     end function wo_release_sigxfsz
  end interface

\eatline
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{106}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: signal_is_pending
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{107}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  function signal_is_pending () result (flag)
    logical :: flag
    flag = &
         wo_sigint /= 0 .or. &
         wo_sigterm /= 0 .or. &
         wo_sigxcpu /= 0 .or. &
         wo_sigxfsz /= 0
  end function signal_is_pending
  
\eatline
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{108}\moddef{Diagnostics: public}\plusendmoddef
  public :: terminate_now_if_signal
\nwendcode{}\nwbegincode{109}\moddef{Diagnostics: procedures}\plusendmoddef
  subroutine terminate_now_if_signal ()
    if (wo_sigint /= 0) then
       call msg_terminate ("Signal SIGINT (keyboard interrupt) received.", &
          quit_code=int (wo_sigint))
    else if (wo_sigterm /= 0) then
       call msg_terminate ("Signal SIGTERM (termination signal) received.", &
          quit_code=int (wo_sigterm))
    else if (wo_sigxcpu /= 0) then
       call msg_terminate ("Signal SIGXCPU (CPU time limit exceeded) received.", &
          quit_code=int (wo_sigxcpu))
    else if (wo_sigxfsz /= 0) then
       call msg_terminate ("Signal SIGXFSZ (file size limit exceeded) received.", &
          quit_code=int (wo_sigxfsz))
    end if
  end subroutine terminate_now_if_signal    

\eatline

\section{Operating-system interface}
For specific purposes, we need direct access to the OS (system
calls).  This is, of course, system dependent.  The current version is
valid for GNU/Linux; we expect to use a preprocessor for this module
if different OSs are to be supported.

The current implementation lacks error handling.
\nwenddocs{}\nwbegincode{111}\moddef{\code{}os{\char95}interface.f90\edoc{}}\endmoddef

module os_interface

  use, intrinsic :: iso_c_binding !NODEP!

\LA{}Use strings\RA{}
  use io_units
  use unit_tests
  use diagnostics
  use system_defs, only: DLERROR_LEN, ENVVAR_LEN
  use system_dependencies
  
\LA{}Standard module head\RA{}

\LA{}OS interface: public\RA{}

\LA{}OS interface: types\RA{}

\LA{}OS interface: interfaces\RA{}

contains

\LA{}OS interface: procedures\RA{}

\LA{}OS interface: tests\RA{}

end module os_interface
\eatline
